text:
We might have officially reached the end of the "just add more compute" AI era.

Top labs are spending billions on larger models, but the performance gains are shrinking fast.

Here is what just happened:

- Spending 10x more training capital now yields less than a 5% bump in raw benchmark scores.
- Top labs are quietly pivoting from massive pre-training to models that "think" longer at inference time.
- The edge is shifting from massive centralized clusters to hyper-efficient niche architectures.

Why this actually matters:
Brute-force scaling is hitting a hard economic ceiling. The winner of the next AI decade won't build the biggest model, but the smartest system.

Are we hitting a temporary AI plateau, or is inference-time compute the real answer?
